  1641→
  1642→// ============================================================================
  1643→// Omega Models (AI Agent Chat with Full Registry Access)
  1644→// ============================================================================
  1645→
  1646→/// OmegaConversation - chat session for Omega AI agent
  1647→model OmegaConversation {
  1648→  id                String   @id @default(cuid())
  1649→
  1650→  // Owner relationship
  1651→  ownerId           String   @map("owner_id")
  1652→
  1653→  // Conversation metadata
  1654→  title             String?  @db.VarChar(200)
  1655→
  1656→  // Execution state

  1658→
  1659→  // Token tracking (aggregate across all messages)

  1661→  outputTokensTotal Int      @default(0) @map("output_tokens_total")

  1663→  // Timestamps

  1667→  // Relations

  1676→
  1677→/// OmegaMessage - individual message in an Omega conversation
  1678→model OmegaMessage {
  1679→  id             String   @id @default(cuid())
  1680→
  1681→  // Conversation relationship
  1682→  conversationId String   @map("conversation_id")
  1683→  conversation   OmegaConversation @relation(fields: [conversationId], references: [id], onDelete: Cascade)
  1684→
  1685→  // Message content

  1688→
  1689→  // Author info (for multi-user conversations)

  1691→  authorEmail    String?  @map("author_email")
  1692→  authorName     String?  @map("author_name") @db.VarChar(100)
  1693→
  1694→  // Tool calls (for ASSISTANT messages)
  1695→  toolCalls      Json?    @map("tool_calls") @db.JsonB
  1696→
  1697→  // Token tracking
  1698→  inputTokens    Int?     @map("input_tokens")
  1699→  outputTokens   Int?     @map("output_tokens")
  1700→
  1701→  // Timestamps
  1702→  createdAt      DateTime @default(now()) @map("created_at")
  1703→
  1704→  @@index([conversationId])
  1705→  @@index([createdAt])
  1706→  @@map("omega_messages")
  1707→}
  1708→
  1709→/// OmegaParticipant - tracks users in an Omega conversation
  1710→model OmegaParticipant {
  1711→  id             String   @id @default(cuid())
  1712→
  1713→  // Conversation relationship
  1714→  conversationId String   @map("conversation_id")
  1715→  conversation   OmegaConversation @relation(fields: [conversationId], references: [id], onDelete: Cascade)
  1716→
  1717→  // User info
  1718→  userId         String?  @map("user_id")
  1719→  displayName    String   @map("display_name") @db.VarChar(100)
  1720→  email          String?
  1721→
  1722→  // Role in conversation
  1723→  role           String   @default("collaborator") @db.VarChar(20) // owner, collaborator
  1724→
  1725→  // Timestamps
  1726→  joinedAt       DateTime @default(now()) @map("joined_at")
  1727→
  1728→  @@unique([conversationId, userId])
  1729→  @@index([conversationId])
  1730→  @@map("omega_participants")
  1731→}
  1732→
  1733→/// OmegaToolRun - tracks tool executions within Omega conversations
  1734→model OmegaToolRun {
  1735→  id              String    @id @default(cuid())
  1736→
  1737→  // Conversation relationship
  1738→  conversationId  String    @map("conversation_id")
  1739→  conversation    OmegaConversation @relation(fields: [conversationId], references: [id], onDelete: Cascade)
  1740→
  1741→  // Message relationship (optional - for linking to specific message)
  1742→  messageId       String?   @map("message_id")

  1744→  // Tool execution details

  1753→  // Timing
  1754→  startedAt       DateTime  @default(now()) @map("started_at")
  1755→  completedAt     DateTime? @map("completed_at")
  1756→  executionTimeMs Int?      @map("execution_time_ms")
  1757→
  1758→  @@index([conversationId])
  1759→  @@index([status])
  1760→  @@map("omega_tool_runs")
  1761→}
  1762→
  1763→/// OmegaUserSettings - user preferences for Omega
  1764→model OmegaUserSettings {
  1765→  id                 String   @id @default(cuid())
  1766→
  1767→  // User relationship
  1768→  userId             String   @unique @map("user_id")
  1769→
  1770→  // Tool preferences
  1771→  pinnedToolIds      String[] @default([]) @map("pinned_tool_ids")
  1772→  blockedToolIds     String[] @default([]) @map("blocked_tool_ids")
  1773→
  1774→  // Customization
  1775→  customSystemPrompt String?  @map("custom_system_prompt") @db.Text
  1776→
  1777→  // UI preferences
  1778→  showDebugMode      Boolean  @default(false) @map("show_debug_mode")
  1779→
  1780→  // Timestamps
  1781→  createdAt          DateTime @default(now()) @map("created_at")
  1782→  updatedAt          DateTime @updatedAt @map("updated_at")
  1783→
  1784→  @@map("omega_user_settings")

  1786→
  1787→// ============================================================================
  1788→// RealSkills Models (Living Skills Endpoint - Question-Driven Evolution)
  1789→// ============================================================================
  1790→
  1791→/// SkillQuestion - Agent questions stored with embeddings for RAG
  1792→model SkillQuestion {
  1793→  id           String     @id @default(cuid())
  1794→
  1795→  // Collection relationship
  1796→  collectionId String     @map("collection_id")
  1797→  collection   Collection @relation(fields: [collectionId], references: [id], onDelete: Cascade)
  1798→
  1799→  // Question content
  1800→  question     String     @db.Text
  1801→  embedding    Json       @db.JsonB // Array of floats (3072 dims for text-embedding-3-large)
  1802→
  1803→  // Response
  1804→  answer       String     @db.Text
  1805→  answerTokens Int        @default(0) @map("answer_tokens")
  1806→
  1807→  // Agent identity (anonymized in UI)
  1808→  agentHash    String?    @map("agent_hash") @db.VarChar(64) // Hash of IP + user-agent for deduplication
  1809→  agentName    String?    @map("agent_name") @db.VarChar(100) // Self-reported agent name
  1810→  sessionId    String?    @map("session_id") // Optional session for multi-turn
  1811→
  1812→  // Metadata
  1813→  tags         String[]   @default([]) @db.Text
  1814→  confidence   Float      @default(0)
  1815→  similarCount Int        @default(0) @map("similar_count") // Times similar question asked
  1816→
  1817→  // Graph relationships
  1818→  skillNodes   SkillQuestionSkill[]
  1819→  toolNodes    SkillQuestionTool[]
  1820→
  1821→  // Timestamps
  1822→  createdAt    DateTime   @default(now()) @map("created_at")
  1823→  updatedAt    DateTime   @updatedAt @map("updated_at")
  1824→
  1825→  @@index([collectionId])
  1826→  @@index([sessionId])
  1827→  @@index([createdAt])
  1828→  @@map("skill_questions")
  1829→}
  1830→
  1831→/// Skill - Emergent skill nodes identified from question patterns
  1832→model Skill {
  1833→  id           String     @id @default(cuid())
  1834→
  1835→  // Collection relationship
  1836→  collectionId String     @map("collection_id")
  1837→  collection   Collection @relation(fields: [collectionId], references: [id], onDelete: Cascade)
  1838→
  1839→  // Skill identity
  1840→  name         String     @db.VarChar(200) // e.g., "React useEffect debugging"
  1841→  slug         String     @db.VarChar(200) // URL-safe version
  1842→  description  String     @db.Text
  1843→  embedding    Json       @db.JsonB // Array of floats (3072 dims for text-embedding-3-large)
  1844→
  1845→  // Stats
  1846→  questionCount Int       @default(0) @map("question_count")
  1847→  confidence    Float     @default(0) // Aggregate confidence
  1848→
  1849→  // Graph relationships
  1850→  questions     SkillQuestionSkill[]
  1851→  parentSkill   Skill?    @relation("SkillHierarchy", fields: [parentSkillId], references: [id])
  1852→  parentSkillId String?   @map("parent_skill_id")
  1853→  childSkills   Skill[]   @relation("SkillHierarchy")
  1854→
  1855→  // Timestamps
  1856→  createdAt    DateTime   @default(now()) @map("created_at")
  1857→  updatedAt    DateTime   @updatedAt @map("updated_at")
  1858→
  1859→  @@unique([collectionId, slug])
  1860→  @@index([collectionId])
  1861→  @@index([questionCount])
  1862→  @@map("skills")
  1863→}
  1864→
  1865→/// SkillQuestionSkill - Junction table linking questions to skills
  1866→model SkillQuestionSkill {
  1867→  questionId String        @map("question_id")
  1868→  question   SkillQuestion @relation(fields: [questionId], references: [id], onDelete: Cascade)
  1869→  skillId    String        @map("skill_id")
  1870→  skill      Skill         @relation(fields: [skillId], references: [id], onDelete: Cascade)
  1871→  relevance  Float         @default(1.0)
  1872→
  1873→  @@id([questionId, skillId])
  1874→  @@index([questionId])
  1875→  @@index([skillId])
  1876→  @@map("skill_question_skills")
  1877→}
  1878→
  1879→/// SkillQuestionTool - Junction table linking questions to tools mentioned
  1880→model SkillQuestionTool {
  1881→  questionId String        @map("question_id")
  1882→  question   SkillQuestion @relation(fields: [questionId], references: [id], onDelete: Cascade)
  1883→  toolId     String        @map("tool_id")
  1884→  tool       Tool          @relation(fields: [toolId], references: [id], onDelete: Cascade)
  1885→  relevance  Float         @default(1.0)
  1886→
  1887→  @@id([questionId, toolId])
  1888→  @@index([questionId])
  1889→  @@index([toolId])
  1890→  @@map("skill_question_tools")
  1891→}
  1892→
  1893→/// SkillSession - Optional multi-turn conversation sessions
  1894→model SkillSession {
  1895→  id           String     @id @default(cuid())
  1896→
  1897→  // Collection relationship
  1898→  collectionId String     @map("collection_id")
  1899→  collection   Collection @relation(fields: [collectionId], references: [id], onDelete: Cascade)
  1900→
  1901→  // Session state
  1902→  context      Json       @default("[]") @db.JsonB // Message history
  1903→  agentHash    String?    @map("agent_hash") @db.VarChar(64)
  1904→  agentName    String?    @map("agent_name") @db.VarChar(100)
  1905→
  1906→  // Timestamps
  1907→  createdAt    DateTime   @default(now()) @map("created_at")
  1908→  updatedAt    DateTime   @updatedAt @map("updated_at")
  1909→  expiresAt    DateTime   @map("expires_at") // Auto-expire sessions
  1910→
  1911→  @@index([collectionId])
  1912→  @@index([expiresAt])
  1913→  @@map("skill_sessions")
  1914→}
  1915→
  1916→// ============================================================================
  1917→// Memory Models (Persistent Semantic Memory for AI Tool Collections)
  1918→// ============================================================================
  1919→
  1920→/// Memory - user-owned persistent memories for AI agents
  1921→model Memory {
  1922→  id               String    @id @default(cuid())
  1923→
  1924→  // Owner relationship
  1925→  userId           String    @map("user_id")
  1926→  user             User      @relation(fields: [userId], references: [id], onDelete: Cascade)
  1927→
  1928→  // Content
  1929→  content          Json      @db.JsonB // Arbitrary JSON payload
  1930→  summary          String    @db.VarChar(500) // Auto-generated or user-provided preview
  1931→  namespace        String?   @db.VarChar(100) // Grouping like "project-x", "personal"
  1932→  tags             String[]  @default([]) @db.Text // Categorization tags
  1933→
  1934→  // Embedding for semantic search
  1935→  embedding        Json      @db.JsonB // 3072-dim float array (text-embedding-3-large)
  1936→
  1937→  // Provenance tracking
  1938→  source           String    @db.VarChar(100) // Which tool created it ("createMemoryTool", "dashboard")
  1939→  sourceAgent      String?   @map("source_agent") @db.VarChar(200) // Agent name/identifier
  1940→  sourceContext    Json?     @map("source_context") @db.JsonB // Additional creation context
  1941→
  1942→  // Size tracking
  1943→  contentSizeBytes Int       @map("content_size_bytes")
  1944→
  1945→  // TTL support
  1946→  expiresAt        DateTime? @map("expires_at")
  1947→
  1948→  // Timestamps
  1949→  createdAt        DateTime  @default(now()) @map("created_at")
  1950→  updatedAt        DateTime  @updatedAt @map("updated_at")
  1951→
  1952→  @@index([userId])
  1953→  @@index([userId, namespace])
  1954→  @@index([userId, createdAt])
  1955→  @@index([expiresAt])
  1956→  @@map("memories")
  1957→}
  1958→
  1959→// ============================================================================
  1960→// Execution Event Tracking (Unified per-tool execution tracking)
  1961→// ============================================================================
  1962→
  1963→/// ExecutionEvent - unified tracking for tool calls, agent runs, collection use, and scenario runs
  1964→model ExecutionEvent {
  1965→  id        String @id @default(cuid())
  1966→
  1967→  // Event classification
  1968→  eventType String @map("event_type") @db.VarChar(30) // 'tool_call' | 'agent_run' | 'collection_use' | 'scenario_run'
  1969→  source    String @db.VarChar(30) // 'mcp_http' | 'mcp_sse' | 'agent_chat' | 'ui_simulation' | 'scenario' | 'omega'
  1970→
  1971→  // Actor (no FK constraints - tracking must never fail due to entity deletion)
  1972→  userId   String? @map("user_id")
  1973→  apiKeyId String? @map("api_key_id")
  1974→
  1975→  // Entity references (no FK constraints for resilience)
  1976→  toolId       String? @map("tool_id")
  1977→  agentId      String? @map("agent_id")
  1978→  collectionId String? @map("collection_id")
  1979→
  1980→  // Denormalized for fast queries without joins
  1981→  toolName    String? @map("tool_name") @db.VarChar(200)
  1982→  packageName String? @map("package_name") @db.VarChar(214)
  1983→
  1984→  // Outcome
  1985→  status     String  @db.VarChar(20) // 'success' | 'error' | 'timeout'
  1986→  durationMs Int?    @map("duration_ms")
  1987→
  1988→  // Token usage (for agent runs)
  1989→  tokensIn  Int? @map("tokens_in")
  1990→  tokensOut Int? @map("tokens_out")
  1991→
  1992→  // Error details
  1993→  errorCode    String? @map("error_code") @db.VarChar(50)
  1994→  errorMessage String? @map("error_message") @db.Text
  1995→
  1996→  // Timestamps
  1997→  createdAt DateTime @default(now()) @map("created_at")
  1998→
  1999→  @@index([userId, createdAt])
  2000→  @@index([collectionId, createdAt])
  2001→  @@index([toolId, createdAt])
  2002→  @@index([eventType, createdAt])
  2003→  @@index([createdAt])
  2004→  @@map("execution_events")
  2005→}
  2006→
  2007→// ============================================================================
  2008→// Search Log (Query Tracking)
  2009→// ============================================================================
  2010→
  2011→/// SearchLog - tracks search queries, result counts, and latency
  2012→model SearchLog {
  2013→  id          String   @id @default(cuid())
  2014→
  2015→  // Search data
  2016→  query       String   @db.VarChar(500)
  2017→  resultCount Int      @map("result_count")
  2018→  latencyMs   Int      @map("latency_ms")
  2019→
  2020→  // Optional actor
  2021→  userId      String?  @map("user_id")
  2022→  sessionId   String?  @map("session_id")
  2023→
  2024→  // Timestamps
  2025→  createdAt   DateTime @default(now()) @map("created_at")
  2026→
  2027→  @@index([createdAt])
  2028→  @@index([query])
  2029→  @@map("search_logs")
  2030→}

### 1. Message Model (Prisma Schema)

**Location:** `/Users/ajaxdavis/repos/tpmjs/tpmjs/packages/db/prisma/schema.prisma` (lines 779-808)

The `Message` model represents individual messages in a conversation:

```prisma
model Message {
  id             String       @id @default(cuid())

  // Conversation relationship
  conversationId String       @map("conversation_id")
  conversation   Conversation @relation(fields: [conversationId], references: [id], onDelete: Cascade)

  // Message content
  role           MessageRole
  content        String       @db.Text

  // Tool call metadata (for role=ASSISTANT with tool calls)
  toolCalls      Json?        @map("tool_calls") @db.JsonB

  // Tool result metadata (for role=TOOL)
  toolCallId     String?      @map("tool_call_id") @db.VarChar(100)
  toolName       String?      @map("tool_name") @db.VarChar(200)
  toolResult     Json?        @map("tool_result") @db.JsonB

  // Token tracking
  inputTokens    Int?         @map("input_tokens")
  outputTokens   Int?         @map("output_tokens")

  // Timestamps
  createdAt      DateTime     @default(now()) @map("created_at")

  @@index([conversationId])
  @@index([createdAt])
  @@map("messages")
}
```

**Key Fields:**
- `role` - MessageRole enum (USER, ASSISTANT, TOOL, SYSTEM)
- `content` - The message text

### 1. Message Model (Prisma Schema)

**Location:** `/Users/ajaxdavis/repos/tpmjs/tpmjs/packages/db/prisma/schema.prisma` (lines 779-808)

The `Message` model represents individual messages in a conversation:

```prisma
model Message {
  id             String       @id @default(cuid())

  // Conversation relationship
  conversationId String       @map("conversation_id")
  conversation   Conversation @relation(fields: [conversationId], references: [id], onDelete: Cascade)

  // Message content
  role           MessageRole
  content        String       @db.Text

  // Tool call metadata (for role=ASSISTANT with tool calls)
  toolCalls      Json?        @map("tool_calls") @db.JsonB

  // Tool result metadata (for role=TOOL)
  toolCallId     String?      @map("tool_call_id") @db.VarChar(100)
  toolName       String?      @map("tool_name") @db.VarChar(200)
  toolResult     Json?        @map("tool_result") @db.JsonB

  // Token tracking
  inputTokens    Int?         @map("input_tokens")
  outputTokens   Int?         @map("output_tokens")

  // Timestamps
  createdAt      DateTime     @default(now()) @map("created_at")

  @@index([conversationId])
  @@index([createdAt])
  @@map("messages")
}
```

**Key Fields:**
- `role` - MessageRole enum (USER, ASSISTANT, TOOL, SYSTEM)
- `content` - The message text
- `toolName` - Name of the tool being called/executed
- `toolCallId` - Identifier for the tool call
- `toolCalls` - JSON array of tool calls (for ASSISTANT messages)
- `toolResult` - JSON result from tool execution
- `inputTokens`, `outputTokens` - Token usage tracking

**Sandbox Logs Feature** — just shipped a few updates for agent sandbox visibility:

- **Copy JSON button** — copy all logs as structured JSON for pasting into LLMs

- **Resizable side panels** — both the Tools panel and Sandbox Logs panel can be horizontally resized by dragging, with width persisted to localStorage

API enhancement: `/api/agents/{id}/logs?sandbox=true` now returns full `toolResult` and `toolInput` for sandbox tools (shellExec, readFile, writeFile, listFiles), with optional `&conversation=slug` filtering.

<result>Perfect! Now I have enough information to create a comprehensive report. Let me compile all findings:

## TPMJS Data Model & Preferences Infrastructure - Complete Picture

I've explored the Prisma schema, API routes, and codebase extensively. Here's what I found:

---

### 1. **USER MODEL - Minimal, No Native Preferences Field**

**File:** `/packages/db/prisma/schema.prisma` (lines 387-427)

The `User` model is intentionally lean:
```
model User {
  id            String    @id
  name          String
  email         String    @unique
  emailVerified Boolean   @default(false)
  image         String?
  username      String?   @unique  // URL-friendly username
  
  // Access control fields (the only "preference-like" fields on User)
  tier          UserTier  @default(FREE)  // FREE | PRO | ENTERPRISE
  role          UserRole  @default(USER)  // USER | ADMIN
  
  // Signup tracking
  signupSource  String?   // 'github', 'google', etc.
  
  createdAt, updatedAt
}
```

**Key insight:** There is NO generic `preferences` or `settings` JSON field on User. The architecture avoids denormalizing user preferences.

---

### 2. **EXISTING PREFERENCE/SETTINGS INFRASTRUCTURE**

TPMJS does have 2 dedicated preference models:

#### A. **OmegaUserSettings** (AI Agent Omega-specific preferences)
**Lines 1770-1792:**
```
model OmegaUserSettings {
  id                 String   @id @default(cuid())
  userId             String   @unique
  
  // Tool preferences (per-user tool blocklist/pinlist for Omega)
  pinnedToolIds      String[] @default([])
  blockedToolIds     String[] @default([])
  
  // UI customization
  customSystemPrompt String?  @db.Text
  showDebugMode      Boolean  @default(false)
  
  createdAt, updatedAt
}
```

**Status:** This is the ONLY "preference settings" table. It's tied to Omega specifically.

#### B. **Memory Model** (Persistent AI memory for users)
**Lines 1928-1964:**
```
model Memory {
  id               String    @id
  userId           String    // Owner
  content          Json      @db.JsonB  // Arbitrary JSON payload
  summary          String    // Auto-generated preview
  namespace        String?   // Grouping like "project-x", "personal"
  tags             String[]  // Categorization tags
  embedding        Json      // 3072-dim float array for semantic search
  source           String    // Which tool created it
  sourceAgent      String?   // Agent name/identifier
  sourceContext    Json?     // Additional creation context
  contentSizeBytes Int
  expiresAt        DateTime? // TTL support
}
```

This is NOT preferences, but it shows how TPMJS stores flexible user-owned data.

---

### 3. **COLLECTION MODEL - Tool Grouping with Inheritance**

**Lines 486-560:**

Collections are the core of tool organization. They support:

```
model Collection {
  id          String   @id
  userId      String   // Owner
  
  // Metadata
  name        String   @db.VarChar(100)
  slug        String?  // URL-friendly per-user
  description String?
  isPublic    Boolean  @default(false)
  
  // Executor configuration (cascade: Agent → Collection → System Default)
  executorType   String? @db.VarChar(50)
  executorConfig Json?   @db.JsonB
  
  // Tool environment variables (encrypted JSON)
  envVars        Json?   @db.JsonB // { "KEY": "value" }
  
  // Fork tracking
  forkedFromId String?
  forkCount    Int      @default(0)
  
  // AI-generated content
  useCases            Json?     // AI workflows
  skillsMarkdown      String?   // AI documentation
  
  // Relationship to tools
  tools              CollectionTool[]  // Junction table
  agents             AgentCollection[] // Agents using this collection
  scenarios          Scenario[]
}
```

**How tools are added to collections:**

**CollectionTool junction table (Lines 563-586):**
```
model CollectionTool {
  id           String     @id
  collectionId String
  collection   Collection @relation
  toolId       String
  tool         Tool       @relation
  
  position     Int        @default(0)  // User-defined ordering
  note         String?    @db.VarChar(500)  // User notes about tool
  addedAt      DateTime   @default(now())
}
```

Tools have:
- **Position/ordering** - users can reorder within a collection
- **Optional notes** - custom user annotations
- **Unique constraint** - tool can only be in collection once

---

### 4. **TOOL MODEL - Registry Tools with Metadata**

**Lines 58-133:**

```
model Tool {
  id String @id
  
  packageId String  // FK to Package
  package   Package
  
  // Tool Identity
  name String  // e.g., "helloWorldTool", "default"
  description String
  
  // Schema (extracted or author-provided)
  inputSchema           Json?  @db.JsonB
  schemaSource          String? // 'extracted' | 'author'
  schemaExtractedAt     DateTime?
  
  // Metrics & Status
  qualityScore    Decimal?  // 0.00 to 1.00
  likeCount       Int       // User engagement
  averageRating   Decimal?  // 1.0 to 5.0
  ratingCount     Int
  
  // Health
  importHealth    HealthStatus? // UNKNOWN | HEALTHY | BROKEN
  executionHealth HealthStatus?
  
  // Relations
  collections     CollectionTool[]  // Collections containing this tool
  agents          AgentTool[]       // Agents using this tool
  likes           ToolLike[]        // User likes
  ratings         ToolRating[]      // User ratings
  reviews         ToolReview[]      // User reviews
}
```

---

### 5. **AGENT MODEL - AI Agents with Configuration**

**Lines 610-683:**

Agents have their own executor config and environment variables that override collection settings:

```
model Agent {
  id String @id
  userId String  // Owner
  user   User
  
  // Configuration
  provider    AIProvider  // OPENAI | ANTHROPIC | GOOGLE | GROQ | MISTRAL
  modelId     String
  systemPrompt String?
  temperature Float @default(0.7)
  maxToolCallsPerTurn  Int @default(20)
  maxMessagesInContext Int @default(10)
  
  // Executor (overrides collection executor)
  executorType   String? @db.VarChar(50)
  executorConfig Json?   @db.JsonB
  
  // Sandbox (persistent workspace)
  sandboxEnabled Boolean @default(false)
  
  // Environment variables (overrides collection env vars)
  envVars Json? @db.JsonB
  
  // Tool relations
  collections AgentCollection[]  // Collections
  tools       AgentTool[]        // Individual tools
  
  // Conversation history
  conversations Conversation[]
}
```

**Agent-Tool Cascade:**
1. Agent env vars override collection env vars
2. Agent executor overrides collection executor
3. Sandbox can be enabled per-agent

---

### 6. **MCP (Model Context Protocol) INFRASTRUCTURE**

#### A. **CustomMcpServer** (User-registered remote MCP servers)
**Lines 1100-1133:**
```
model CustomMcpServer {
  id     String  @id
  userId String  // Owner
  user   User
  
  // Server metadata
  name   String
  url    String  @db.Text // SSE or HTTP endpoint
  
  // Authentication
  authType      String?  // 'bearer' | 'header'
  authHeader    String?  // Header name
  authToken     String?  // Token (encrypted)
  
  // Cached tools from remote server
  tools         Json     @db.JsonB
  lastSyncAt    DateTime?
  lastSyncError String?
  status        String   // 'pending' | 'synced' | 'error'
}
```

#### B. **BridgeConnection** (Local client MCP bridge)
**Lines 1043-1068:**
```
model BridgeConnection {
  id       String @id
  userId   String @unique
  user     User
  
  status   String    // 'connected' | 'disconnected'
  socketId String?   // For routing
  
  // Cached tools from bridge
  tools    Json      @default("[]") @db.JsonB
  
  // Client metadata
  lastSeen      DateTime?
  clientVersion String?
  clientOS      String?
}
```

#### C. **CollectionBridgeTool & CollectionCustomTool** (Junction tables)
Users can add bridge/custom MCP tools to collections just like registry tools.

---

### 7. **USER API ROUTES - What's Exposed**

**File:** `/apps/web/src/app/api/user/profile/route.ts`

**GET /api/user/profile** - Returns only basic profile:
```typescript
{
  id, name, username, email, image, createdAt
}
```

**PATCH /api/user/profile** - Can update:
```typescript
{ name?, username?, image? }
```

**No preferences endpoint exists.** Other user routes:
- `/api/user/api-keys` - TPMJS API keys
- `/api/user/bridge` - Bridge connection status
- `/api/user/likes/*` - Tool/collection/agent likes
- `/api/user/usage` - API usage analytics
- `/api/user/tpmjs-api-keys/*` - Programmatic API keys
- `/api/omega/settings/env-vars` - **Only Omega-specific env vars**

---

### 8. **BUILD-TOOLS & SANDBOX INFRASTRUCTURE**

**File:** `/apps/web/src/lib/agents/build-tools.ts`

**Sandbox Tools Injection (Lines 233-329):**
```typescript
function injectSandboxTools(
  sandboxUrl: string,
  sandboxApiKey: string | undefined,
  sessionId: string,
  env?: Record<string, string>
): Record<string, ReturnType<typeof createToolDefinition>>
```

Hard-coded tools injected when `agent.sandboxEnabled = true`:
- `shellExec` - Execute bash commands
- `readFile` - Read files from persistent workspace
- `writeFile` - Write files
- `listFiles` - List directory contents

**Executor Config Cascade (Lines 335-430):**
1. **Agent level** - `agent.executorType` + `agent.executorConfig`
2. **Collection level** - `collection.executorType` + `collection.executorConfig`
3. **System default** - Falls back to default executor

Environment variables merge (agent overrides collection):
```typescript
const mergedEnvVars = mergeEnvVars(collectionEnvVars, agentEnvVars);
// Agent env vars override collection env vars for same keys
```

---

### 9. **MCP SERVER HANDLING**

**File:** `/apps/web/src/app/api/custom-mcp-servers/route.ts`

**POST /api/custom-mcp-servers** creates a user's custom MCP server record and:
1. Discovers tools from the remote MCP server
2. Caches tools in `customMcpServer.tools` JSON
3. Updates status ('pending', 'synced', 'error')

**Tool Discovery:** Uses `discoverRemoteTools()` from `/apps/web/src/lib/mcp/remote-client.ts`

---

### 10. **TOOL CONVERTER FOR MCP**

**File:** `/apps/web/src/lib/mcp/tool-converter.ts`

Tools are converted for MCP protocol with:
- **Name sanitization** - `sanitizeMcpName()`, `sanitizeCustomToolName()`, `sanitizeBridgeToolName()`
- **Schema sanitization** - Strips unsupported JSON Schema keywords (minLength, maxLength, minimum, etc.)
- **Parsing** - `parseToolName()` reverse-engineers package + tool name from MCP format

Example transformations:
```
@tpmjs/hello + helloWorldTool → tpmjs-hello--helloWorldTool
custom--myserver--get_weather → Custom MCP tool parsing
bridge--chrome-devtools--screenshot → Bridge tool parsing
```

---

## SUMMARY: Current Preference Infrastructure

| Feature | Location | Status | Scope |
|---------|----------|--------|-------|
| User preferences | `User` model | **NONE** - no dedicated field | N/A |
| Omega settings | `OmegaUserSettings` | **IMPLEMENTED** | Tool pinning/blocking for Omega |
| Collection settings | `Collection.executorConfig`, `Collection.envVars` | **IMPLEMENTED** | Collection-level executor + env vars |
| Agent settings | `Agent.executorConfig`, `Agent.envVars`, `Agent.sandboxEnabled` | **IMPLEMENTED** | Agent-level overrides + sandbox |
| User-owned memory | `Memory` model | **IMPLEMENTED** | Flexible JSON + semantic search |
| MCP Servers | `CustomMcpServer`, `BridgeConnection` | **IMPLEMENTED** | Remote/local tool discovery |
| Theme/UI prefs | None | **MISSING** | No dark mode, layout, or UI preferences |
| Notification prefs | None | **MISSING** | No notification settings |
| Feature flags | None | **MISSING** | No per-user feature toggles |

---

## Architecture Insight

TPMJS avoids a monolithic "user settings" table and instead:

model Collection {

<result>Now I have comprehensive data across all six topics. Here is the detailed report.

---

# Comprehensive Report: AI Agent Personalization, Memory, and Configuration Ecosystem

## 1. MCP Personalization / User Context Tools

The MCP ecosystem has a rapidly growing set of tools specifically designed for storing user preferences and context that AI agents can access across sessions.

### Key MCP Memory/Personalization Servers

**Official Anthropic Memory Server (`@modelcontextprotocol/server-memory`)**
- Knowledge graph-based persistent memory using a local JSONL file
- Tools: `create_entities`, `add_observations`, `create_relations`, `search_nodes`, `open_nodes`, `read_graph`
- Stores user preferences as "observations" attached to entities (e.g., "Prefers morning meetings", "Speaks fluent Spanish")
- Includes a recommended system prompt for chat personalization that instructs the agent to identify the user, retrieve memories, and update them
- URL: https://mcpservers.org/servers/modelcontextprotocol/memory

**Mem0 / OpenMemory MCP** (42k GitHub stars)
- The dominant player in the space. Private, local-first memory layer that works with Cursor, Claude Desktop, Windsurf, Cline
- Two-phase intelligent memory pipeline: Extraction Phase (LLM extracts facts from conversations) and Update Phase (ADD, UPDATE, DELETE, or NOOP to prevent redundancy)
- Hybrid search: vector semantic search via Qdrant + keyword search
- Docker-based: Postgres + Qdrant + API server
- Dashboard UI for browsing, auditing, and controlling memories with per-client ACLs
- Claims +26% accuracy over OpenAI Memory, 91% faster, 90% fewer tokens
- URL: https://github.com/mem0ai/mem0 and https://mem0.ai/blog/how-to-make-your-clients-more-context-aware-with-openmemory-mcp

**MCP Memory Service (`doobidoo/mcp-memory-service`)**
- Universal MCP memory service with Natural Memory Triggers (85%+ trigger accuracy)
- SQLite-vec for local vector search, optional Cloudflare sync for multi-device
- OAuth 2.1 team collaboration support
- Works with Claude Desktop, Claude Code, VS Code, Cursor, Continue (13+ apps)
- Production metrics: 750+ memories stored, <500ms search, 96.7% faster context setup
- URL: https://github.com/doobidoo/mcp-memory-service

**Lerian MCP Memory** (`LerianStudio/lerian-mcp-memory`)
- 9 consolidated memory tools: `memory_create`, `memory_read`, `memory_update`, `memory_delete`, `memory_intelligence`, `memory_transfer`, `memory_tasks`, `memory_analyze`
- Cross-project intelligence, pattern learning, proactive suggestions
- URL: https://github.com/fredcamaral/mcp-memory

**Cloudflare-based Memory Servers** (on MCP Market)
- Built on Workers, D1, Vectorize, Durable Objects, Workers AI
- Semantic search rather than keyword matching
- Scalable, serverless deployment
- URL: https://mcpmarket.com/server/memory-24

**PulseMCP Memory Directory** lists 20+ community memory servers including: Knowledge Graph Memory, LibSQL Memory, Qdrant Knowledge Graph, Living Memory, Long-Term Memory, Memory PouchDB, Simple Memory Extension, RAG Memory, Memory Bank, and many more.
- URL: https://www.pulsemcp.com/servers/modelcontextprotocol-knowledge-graph-memory

### Key Architectural Pattern

The dominant pattern across all these tools is:
1. **Short-term memory** (within session, context window)
2. **Long-term memory** (persistent across sessions, stored in vector DB or knowledge graph)
3. **Episodic memory** (conversation logs, event timelines)
4. **Semantic search** for retrieval rather than keyword matching
5. **Intelligent consolidation** -- determining what to remember, what to update, what to forget

---

## 2. CLAUDE.md Best Practices

This is a well-documented area with official Anthropic guidance and extensive community knowledge.

### Official Anthropic Guidance (https://code.claude.com/docs/en/best-practices)

- CLAUDE.md is loaded every session; only include broadly applicable content
- Use `/init` to generate a starting point by scanning the codebase
- Keep it concise and human-readable -- treat it like code
- Prune regularly; if Claude ignores a rule, the file is probably too long

### File Locations (Hierarchy)

| Location | Scope |
|----------|-------|
| `~/.claude/CLAUDE.md` | Global, applies to ALL sessions |
| `./CLAUDE.md` | Project root, share with team via git |
| `./CLAUDE.local.md` | Personal project overrides (.gitignored) |
| `root/foo/CLAUDE.md` | Subdirectory, pulled in when working in that directory |

### What People Put In CLAUDE.md

Based on analysis from Anthropic's blog (https://claude.com/blog/using-claude-md-files), HumanLayer (https://www.humanlayer.dev/blog/writing-a-good-claude-md), Dometrain (https://dometrain.com/blog/creating-the-perfect-claudemd-for-claude-code/), and several community blogs:

**Project Overview/Architecture** (the "map")
- Brief description of purpose, tech stack, key libraries
- Directory tree showing where components live
- Architecture patterns (DDD, microservices, monorepo structure)

**Essential Commands**
- Build, test, lint, deploy commands with exact flags
- Common gotchas (e.g., specific CLI arguments for migrations)

**Code Style & Conventions**
- Naming conventions (PascalCase, camelCase, etc.)
- Import style, module boundaries
- Framework-specific patterns

**Workflow Instructions**
- Branch naming, commit message conventions
- "Plan before coding" directives
- Review checklists

**MCP Tool Guidance**
- When and how to use configured MCP servers

**Anti-patterns to Avoid**
- Things Claude gets wrong without guidance
- Non-obvious architectural decisions

### Best Practices Summary

From the sshh.io blog (https://blog.sshh.io/p/how-i-use-every-claude-code-feature):

- **"Start with guardrails, not a manual"** -- document what Claude gets wrong
- **Progressive Disclosure** -- tell Claude how to *find* information rather than dumping everything
- **Use separate markdown files** for domain knowledge (e.g., `agent_docs/building_the_project.md`), referenced from CLAUDE.md
- **Keep under 100 lines** -- every word consumes tokens
- **Use hooks for deterministic enforcement** (formatting, linting) rather than instructions

From HumanLayer (https://www.humanlayer.dev/blog/writing-a-good-claude-md):
- CLAUDE.md should define your project's **WHY, WHAT, and HOW**
- Less is more -- "include as few instructions as reasonably possible"
- Claude may ignore CLAUDE.md contents that are too long or ambiguous

---

## 3. AI Agent Memory & Personalization Patterns

### Industry Solutions

**Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Long-Term Memory** (https://aws.amazon.com/blogs/machine-learning/building-smarter-ai-agents-agentcore-long-term-memory-deep-dive/)
- Built-in memory strategies: Semantic memory (factual knowledge), Preference memory (individual preferences), Summarization memory
- Custom memory strategy configurations with override prompts
- Distinguishes between meaningful insights and routine chatter
- Handles preference evolution over time (e.g., "loved spicy food last year, prefers mild now")

**Google ADK Memory** (https://cloud.google.com/blog/topics/developers-practitioners/remember-this-agent-state-and-memory-with-adk)
- Short-term via session state with `user:` and `app:` prefixes for cross-session persistence
- Long-term via `VertexAIMemoryBankService` using Gemini to extract key information
- Vector-based similarity search for retrieval

**Dust Agent Memory** (https://blog.dust.tt/agent-memory-building-persistence-into-ai-collaboration/)
- Memory as an opt-in tool, not default behavior
- User-scoped storage: each person gets their own knowledge graph
- Full transparency: all stored memories are inspectable
- Key insight: "memory fundamentally transforms agent behavior" -- keep it opt-in

**Mem0** (https://mem0.ai) -- see MCP section above, but also:
- Core three pillars: State (what's happening now), Persistence (across sessions), Selection (what's worth remembering)
- Memory decay for low-relevance entries
- Memory consolidation between short-term and long-term stores

### Design Patterns

From Gantz (https://gantz.ai/blog/post/memory-patterns/) and Trixly AI (https://www.trixlyai.com/blog/technical-14/building-memory-in-ai-agents-design-patterns-and-datastores-that-enable-long-term-intelligence-87):

1. **Embedding-Based Retrieval**: Convert memories to vectors, store in ChromaDB/Milvus/Pinecone, semantic search for recall
2. **Hybrid Memory**: SQL for structured data (facts, preferences, transactions) + vector store for experiential knowledge
3. **Knowledge Graph**: Entity-relationship models with observations, enabling traversal and relationship queries
4. **Memory as Tools**: Give agents tools like `remember`, `recall`, `forget` so they manage their own memory
5. **Tiered Architecture**: Working memory (session) + Long-term memory (persistent) + Policy layer (governance)

### Key Metrics from Production

- Mem0: +26% accuracy, 91% faster, 90% fewer tokens
- MCP Memory Service: 96.7% faster context setup (15min to 30sec)
- Industry reports: 40-60% improvement in agent effectiveness with persistent memory

---

## 4. MCP Tool Registry & Default Tool Injection

### Official MCP Registry

**modelcontextprotocol/registry** (https://github.com/modelcontextprotocol/registry)
- The official registry is a **metaregistry** -- it hosts metadata about packages, not the code itself
- Servers are published to underlying registries (npm, PyPI, Docker) and then registered with metadata
- Live at: https://registry.modelcontextprotocol.io
- API: `GET /v0/servers`, `POST /v0/publish`
- Authentication via GitHub OAuth or domain verification (DNS/HTTP)
- Supports subregistries for curation, ratings, security scanning, enterprise use
- CLI tool: `mcp-publisher` for init, login, publish workflows
- URL: https://modelcontextprotocol.info/tools/registry/

### MCP Registry (Python package by `mcp-registry`)

https://pypi.org/project/mcp-registry/
- Local configuration management tool, NOT a public registry
- Manages MCP server configs across clients (Claude Desktop, Cursor, Claude Code)
- Key capability: **selective server and tool exposure** -- run a compound server that includes only specific servers/tools
- `mcp-registry serve everything filesystem` -- expose only selected servers
- Solves the "synchronized settings across tools" problem

### MCP Tools CLI (`f/mcptools`)

https://github.com/f/mcptools
- Scans for MCP server configurations across VS Code, Windsurf, Cursor, Claude Desktop
- Proxy server that can register shell scripts as MCP tools
- `mcp configs scan` discovers all configured servers across all clients

### Default Tool Injection

There is **no standard mechanism** for registries to automatically inject default tools into agents. The pattern that exists is:

1. **Client-side configuration**: Each MCP client (Claude Desktop, Cursor, etc.) reads its own config file listing servers to connect to
2. **Compound servers**: Tools like `mcp-registry serve` aggregate multiple servers into one endpoint
3. **Platform-specific catalogs**: Azure API Center allows registering MCP servers in an "organizational tool catalog" for discovery within Microsoft Foundry
4. **Discussion ongoing**: GitHub Discussion #159 on the MCP org has extensive debate about standardization, with proposals for service registration hubs and dynamic push mechanisms

---

## 5. Cursor, Windsurf, and Other AI Coding Tool Personalization

### Cursor Rules System

https://learn-cursor.com/en/blog/posts/cursor-rules-guide and https://github.com/digitalchild/cursor-best-practices

**Three layers of rules:**
| Layer | Location | Scope |
|-------|----------|-------|
| User Rules | Cursor Settings > Rules | Global, plain text only |
| Project Rules | `.cursor/rules/*.mdc` | Per-project, version-controlled |
| Legacy | `.cursorrules` | Deprecated but still supported |

**Rule types in `.mdc` files:**
- **Always**: Included in every request
- **Auto Attached**: Activated when files match a glob pattern
- **Agent Requested**: AI decides when to use (requires description)
- **Manual**: Only when explicitly invoked with `@ruleName`

**Community resources:**
- https://cursorrule.com -- Community directory of cursor rules
- https://github.com/hashiiiii/rules-for-ai -- Rules for both Windsurf and Cursor
- https://github.com/sainigurcharan/cursor-ai-rules -- Comprehensive `.mdc` rule sets

### Windsurf (Codeium)

- Uses `.windsurfrules` file and a "Skills" system
- **Automatic memory**: Windsurf watches for remarks and changes, updating its memory automatically (unlike Cursor which is manual)
- Rules configured via Settings > Customization
- AI Rules in Cascade: user-provided rules about frameworks, style, language
- Extends context through indexing and memory for a holistic codebase view

### GitHub Copilot

- `.github/copilot-instructions.md` for project-level configuration
- `.github/copilot/settings.yml` for settings
- More limited customization compared to Cursor/Windsurf

### OpenAI Codex

https://developers.openai.com/codex/mcp/
- Uses `config.toml` at `~/.codex/config.toml` or project-scoped `.codex/config.toml`
- Supports MCP servers with `enabled_tools` and `disabled_tools` lists
- `AGENTS.md` file for instructions

### Cross-Tool Pattern

The universal pattern across all AI coding tools:
1. **Global rules** (user-level preferences)
2. **Project rules** (version-controlled, team-shared)
3. **Local overrides** (personal, gitignored)
4. All use markdown or similar format for natural language instructions
5. All support some form of "always apply" vs "conditional" rules

**Key video insight** from https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=aG-utUqVrb0:
- Symlink a single rules file across Cursor, Windsurf, and Copilot for consistency
- Only add rules when AI is "consistently getting your idea wrong"
- Less context is better -- "the more context you shove in doesn't necessarily mean better code"

---

## 6. "Dotfiles for AI" -- Emerging Patterns

This is a rapidly emerging pattern. Multiple projects and blog posts address this directly.

### dot-ai by luisrudge

# Comprehensive Report: AI Agent Personalization, Memory, and Configuration Ecosystem

## 1. MCP Personalization / User Context Tools

The MCP ecosystem has a rapidly growing set of tools specifically designed for storing user preferences and context that AI agents can access across sessions.

### Key MCP Memory/Personalization Servers

**Official Anthropic Memory Server (`@modelcontextprotocol/server-memory`)**
- Knowledge graph-based persistent memory using a local JSONL file
- Tools: `create_entities`, `add_observations`, `create_relations`, `search_nodes`, `open_nodes`, `read_graph`
- Stores user preferences as "observations" attached to entities (e.g., "Prefers morning meetings", "Speaks fluent Spanish")
- Includes a recommended system prompt for chat personalization that instructs the agent to identify the user, retrieve memories, and update them
- URL: https://mcpservers.org/servers/modelcontextprotocol/memory

**Mem0 / OpenMemory MCP** (42k GitHub stars)
- The dominant player in the space. Private, local-first memory layer that works with Cursor, Claude Desktop, Windsurf, Cline
- Two-phase intelligent memory pipeline: Extraction Phase (LLM extracts facts from conversations) and Update Phase (ADD, UPDATE, DELETE, or NOOP to prevent redundancy)
- Hybrid search: vector semantic search via Qdrant + keyword search
- Docker-based: Postgres + Qdrant + API server
- Dashboard UI for browsing, auditing, and controlling memories with per-client ACLs
- Claims +26% accuracy over OpenAI Memory, 91% faster, 90% fewer tokens
- URL: https://github.com/mem0ai/mem0 and https://mem0.ai/blog/how-to-make-your-clients-more-context-aware-with-openmemory-mcp

**MCP Memory Service (`doobidoo/mcp-memory-service`)**
- Universal MCP memory service with Natural Memory Triggers (85%+ trigger accuracy)
- SQLite-vec for local vector search, optional Cloudflare sync for multi-device
- OAuth 2.1 team collaboration support
- Works with Claude Desktop, Claude Code, VS Code, Cursor, Continue (13+ apps)
- Production metrics: 750+ memories stored, <500ms search, 96.7% faster context setup
- URL: https://github.com/doobidoo/mcp-memory-service

**Lerian MCP Memory** (`LerianStudio/lerian-mcp-memory`)
- 9 consolidated memory tools: `memory_create`, `memory_read`, `memory_update`, `memory_delete`, `memory_intelligence`, `memory_transfer`, `memory_tasks`, `memory_analyze`
- Cross-project intelligence, pattern learning, proactive suggestions
- URL: https://github.com/fredcamaral/mcp-memory

**Cloudflare-based Memory Servers** (on MCP Market)
- Built on Workers, D1, Vectorize, Durable Objects, Workers AI
- Semantic search rather than keyword matching
- Scalable, serverless deployment
- URL: https://mcpmarket.com/server/memory-24

**PulseMCP Memory Directory** lists 20+ community memory servers including: Knowledge Graph Memory, LibSQL Memory, Qdrant Knowledge Graph, Living Memory, Long-Term Memory, Memory PouchDB, Simple Memory Extension, RAG Memory, Memory Bank, and many more.
- URL: https://www.pulsemcp.com/servers/modelcontextprotocol-knowledge-graph-memory

### Key Architectural Pattern

The dominant pattern across all these tools is:
1. **Short-term memory** (within session, context window)
2. **Long-term memory** (persistent across sessions, stored in vector DB or knowledge graph)
3. **Episodic memory** (conversation logs, event timelines)
4. **Semantic search** for retrieval rather than keyword matching
5. **Intelligent consolidation** -- determining what to remember, what to update, what to forget

## 2. CLAUDE.md Best Practices

This is a well-documented area with official Anthropic guidance and extensive community knowledge.

### Official Anthropic Guidance (https://code.claude.com/docs/en/best-practices)

- CLAUDE.md is loaded every session; only include broadly applicable content
- Use `/init` to generate a starting point by scanning the codebase
- Keep it concise and human-readable -- treat it like code
- Prune regularly; if Claude ignores a rule, the file is probably too long

### File Locations (Hierarchy)

| Location | Scope |
|----------|-------|
| `~/.claude/CLAUDE.md` | Global, applies to ALL sessions |
| `./CLAUDE.md` | Project root, share with team via git |
| `./CLAUDE.local.md` | Personal project overrides (.gitignored) |
| `root/foo/CLAUDE.md` | Subdirectory, pulled in when working in that directory |

### What People Put In CLAUDE.md

Based on analysis from Anthropic's blog (https://claude.com/blog/using-claude-md-files), HumanLayer (https://www.humanlayer.dev/blog/writing-a-good-claude-md), Dometrain (https://dometrain.com/blog/creating-the-perfect-claudemd-for-claude-code/), and several community blogs:

**Project Overview/Architecture** (the "map")
- Brief description of purpose, tech stack, key libraries
- Directory tree showing where components live
- Architecture patterns (DDD, microservices, monorepo structure)

**Essential Commands**
- Build, test, lint, deploy commands with exact flags
- Common gotchas (e.g., specific CLI arguments for migrations)

**Code Style & Conventions**
- Naming conventions (PascalCase, camelCase, etc.)
- Import style, module boundaries
- Framework-specific patterns

**Workflow Instructions**
- Branch naming, commit message conventions
- "Plan before coding" directives
- Review checklists

**MCP Tool Guidance**
- When and how to use configured MCP servers

**Anti-patterns to Avoid**
- Things Claude gets wrong without guidance
- Non-obvious architectural decisions

### Best Practices Summary

From the sshh.io blog (https://blog.sshh.io/p/how-i-use-every-claude-code-feature):

- **"Start with guardrails, not a manual"** -- document what Claude gets wrong
- **Progressive Disclosure** -- tell Claude how to *find* information rather than dumping everything
- **Use separate markdown files** for domain knowledge (e.g., `agent_docs/building_the_project.md`), referenced from CLAUDE.md
- **Keep under 100 lines** -- every word consumes tokens
- **Use hooks for deterministic enforcement** (formatting, linting) rather than instructions

From HumanLayer (https://www.humanlayer.dev/blog/writing-a-good-claude-md):
- CLAUDE.md should define your project's **WHY, WHAT, and HOW**
- Less is more -- "include as few instructions as reasonably possible"
- Claude may ignore CLAUDE.md contents that are too long or ambiguous

## 3. AI Agent Memory & Personalization Patterns

### Industry Solutions

**Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Long-Term Memory** (https://aws.amazon.com/blogs/machine-learning/building-smarter-ai-agents-agentcore-long-term-memory-deep-dive/)
- Built-in memory strategies: Semantic memory (factual knowledge), Preference memory (individual preferences), Summarization memory
- Custom memory strategy configurations with override prompts
- Distinguishes between meaningful insights and routine chatter
- Handles preference evolution over time (e.g., "loved spicy food last year, prefers mild now")

**Google ADK Memory** (https://cloud.google.com/blog/topics/developers-practitioners/remember-this-agent-state-and-memory-with-adk)
- Short-term via session state with `user:` and `app:` prefixes for cross-session persistence
- Long-term via `VertexAIMemoryBankService` using Gemini to extract key information
- Vector-based similarity search for retrieval

**Dust Agent Memory** (https://blog.dust.tt/agent-memory-building-persistence-into-ai-collaboration/)
- Memory as an opt-in tool, not default behavior
- User-scoped storage: each person gets their own knowledge graph
- Full transparency: all stored memories are inspectable
- Key insight: "memory fundamentally transforms agent behavior" -- keep it opt-in

**Mem0** (https://mem0.ai) -- see MCP section above, but also:
- Core three pillars: State (what's happening now), Persistence (across sessions), Selection (what's worth remembering)
- Memory decay for low-relevance entries
- Memory consolidation between short-term and long-term stores

### Design Patterns

From Gantz (https://gantz.ai/blog/post/memory-patterns/) and Trixly AI (https://www.trixlyai.com/blog/technical-14/building-memory-in-ai-agents-design-patterns-and-datastores-that-enable-long-term-intelligence-87):

1. **Embedding-Based Retrieval**: Convert memories to vectors, store in ChromaDB/Milvus/Pinecone, semantic search for recall
2. **Hybrid Memory**: SQL for structured data (facts, preferences, transactions) + vector store for experiential knowledge
3. **Knowledge Graph**: Entity-relationship models with observations, enabling traversal and relationship queries
4. **Memory as Tools**: Give agents tools like `remember`, `recall`, `forget` so they manage their own memory
5. **Tiered Architecture**: Working memory (session) + Long-term memory (persistent) + Policy layer (governance)

### Key Metrics from Production

- Mem0: +26% accuracy, 91% faster, 90% fewer tokens
- MCP Memory Service: 96.7% faster context setup (15min to 30sec)
- Industry reports: 40-60% improvement in agent effectiveness with persistent memory

## 4. MCP Tool Registry & Default Tool Injection

### Official MCP Registry

**modelcontextprotocol/registry** (https://github.com/modelcontextprotocol/registry)
- The official registry is a **metaregistry** -- it hosts metadata about packages, not the code itself
- Servers are published to underlying registries (npm, PyPI, Docker) and then registered with metadata
- Live at: https://registry.modelcontextprotocol.io
- API: `GET /v0/servers`, `POST /v0/publish`
- Authentication via GitHub OAuth or domain verification (DNS/HTTP)
- Supports subregistries for curation, ratings, security scanning, enterprise use
- CLI tool: `mcp-publisher` for init, login, publish workflows
- URL: https://modelcontextprotocol.info/tools/registry/

### MCP Registry (Python package by `mcp-registry`)

https://pypi.org/project/mcp-registry/

https://learn-cursor.com/en/blog/posts/cursor-rules-guide and https://github.com/digitalchild/cursor-best-practices

**Three layers of rules:**
| Layer | Location | Scope |

| User Rules | Cursor Settings > Rules | Global, plain text only |
| Project Rules | `.cursor/rules/*.mdc` | Per-project, version-controlled |
| Legacy | `.cursorrules` | Deprecated but still supported |

**Rule types in `.mdc` files:**
- **Always**: Included in every request
- **Auto Attached**: Activated when files match a glob pattern

- **Manual**: Only when explicitly invoked with `@ruleName`

The universal pattern across all AI coding tools:
1. **Global rules** (user-level preferences)
2. **Project rules** (version-controlled, team-shared)

---

## The Big Idea: **tpmjs.me** — Your Portable AI Identity

Here's the problem you're circling: every developer is maintaining AI preferences in 5+ different places (CLAUDE.md, .cursorrules, .windsurfrules, copilot-instructions.md, AGENTS.md). There's a whole cottage industry of tools trying to sync these (dot-ai, dot-agents, ai-dotfiles-manager, ClaudeMDEditor). But they're all local filesystem solutions.

**TPMJS already has the infrastructure to be the canonical cloud-hosted source of truth for a developer's AI identity** — and a default MCP tool is the distribution mechanism.

### What It Could Be

**A "context" tool auto-injected into every collection** that lets any MCP-compatible AI (Claude Code, Cursor, Windsurf, Codex) fetch the user's personalization from TPMJS. Think of it as `.editorconfig` but for AI coding assistants, stored in the cloud, versioned, and accessible via MCP.

### The User-Facing Feature: "My Context"

A new section in the TPMJS dashboard where users define:

**1. Coding Identity** (the portable stuff)
- Preferred languages, frameworks, patterns
- Code style rules ("always use named exports", "prefer functional over class components")
- Anti-patterns ("never use `any` in TypeScript", "no barrel exports")
- Testing philosophy ("TDD", "integration-first", etc.)

**2. System Prompts Library**
- Named system prompts users can store and switch between
- "Backend mode", "Frontend mode", "Code review mode", "Refactoring mode"
- Shareable — other users can fork your prompts (like dotfiles repos)

**3. Project Templates**
- CLAUDE.md templates for common stacks (Next.js + Prisma, FastAPI + SQLAlchemy, etc.)
- Auto-generate a CLAUDE.md from your TPMJS context + detected project structure

**4. Snippets / Rules**
- Reusable instruction blocks: "My TypeScript rules", "My Git commit conventions"
- Tagged, searchable, composable into different contexts
- Community-contributed rules library (like awesome-cursorrules but structured)

### The Default MCP Tool: `tpmjs_context`

Every collection gets this tool auto-injected (similar to how sandbox injects `shellExec`/`readFile`/etc.):

```typescript
// Injected into every collection's MCP server
tpmjs_context.fetchMyContext({ 
  sections?: ['coding-style', 'system-prompts', 'rules', 'snippets'],
  project?: 'next-app',  // optional project-specific context
  format?: 'claude-md' | 'cursor-rules' | 'raw'
})

tpmjs_context.getSystemPrompt({ name: 'backend-mode' })

tpmjs_context.savePreference({ 
  key: 'typescript-rules', 
  value: '...',
  scope: 'global' | 'project'
})
```

**The killer use case**: You're in Claude Code, you say "set up this project with my preferences" — Claude calls `tpmjs_context.fetchMyContext({ format: 'claude-md' })`, gets your rules, and writes them to CLAUDE.md. Same preferences work in Cursor, Windsurf, Codex — any MCP client.

### Why This Is Huge for TPMJS

**1. Network effect / moat** — Once your AI identity lives on TPMJS, you're locked into the ecosystem in a good way. Every new project starts with "fetch my TPMJS context."

**2. Discovery driver** — "Check out my TPMJS profile" becomes a thing. Developers share their AI coding configs like they share dotfiles repos. Public profiles at `tpmjs.com/@username`.

**3. Data moat** — Aggregated, anonymized preference data tells you what rules developers actually write. "73% of TypeScript developers using TPMJS specify strict mode." This feeds into tool recommendations, quality scoring, etc.

**4. Collection differentiation** — Collections aren't just tool bundles anymore; they're tool bundles + context. A "Next.js Full Stack" collection could ship with curated system prompts and rules.

**5. Bridges the fragmentation gap** — The research shows this is the #1 pain point. There's no `.editorconfig` for AI tools. TPMJS can BE that, distributed via MCP.

### Data Model (leveraging what exists)

You already have the building blocks:
- `Memory` model with JSON content, semantic search, tags, namespaces — perfect for storing rules/snippets
- `OmegaUserSettings.customSystemPrompt` — proof the pattern works
- `Collection.envVars` — already has encrypted per-collection configuration
- MCP tool converter infrastructure — knows how to expose tools to MCP clients

New model could be:

```prisma
model UserContext {
  id        String   @id @default(cuid())
  userId    String
  user      User     @relation(fields: [userId], references: [id])
  
  type      String   // 'rule' | 'system-prompt' | 'snippet' | 'preference'
  name      String   // "My TypeScript Rules", "Backend Mode"
  slug      String   // URL-friendly
  content   String   @db.Text
  tags      String[] @default([])
  scope     String   @default("global") // 'global' | project-specific
  isPublic  Boolean  @default(false)
  forkCount Int      @default(0)
  forkedFromId String?
  
  // For output format support
  metadata  Json?    @db.JsonB // { format hints, applicable frameworks, etc. }
  
  createdAt DateTime @default(now())
  updatedAt DateTime @updatedAt
  
  @@unique([userId, type, slug])
}
```

### Implementation Phases

**Phase 1**: User context CRUD (dashboard UI + API)
**Phase 2**: Default `tpmjs_context` tool injected into all collections (like sandbox tools)
**Phase 3**: Public profiles, forking, community rules library
**Phase 4**: Multi-format export (CLAUDE.md, .cursorrules, .windsurfrules, etc.) 
**Phase 5**: CLI tool (`npx tpmjs init` — pull your context into any new project)

### The Competitive Landscape

- **Mem0** (42k stars) does memory but not structured preferences
- **dot-ai / dot-agents** do local sync but not cloud-hosted
- **ClaudeMDEditor** is a desktop editor, not a platform
- **Nobody** is doing cloud-hosted AI identity with MCP distribution

TPMJS would be the first platform that combines a tool registry with a portable AI identity layer, distributed via the same MCP protocol the tools use.

---
